turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Two to three meter surf rolled in and took part of the Hotel San Cristóbal with it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Twelve beachfront rooms damaged, operations suspended for now.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No one hurt, yet the building stands empty while they check the tide line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It stirs the old question of how near we build to the moving shore.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias notes the hotel sits on Punta Lobos beach in Todos Santos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The National Weather Service already warned of exactly that swell across the whole Pacific side, from Guerrero Negro down through Todos Santos and El Pescadero.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 30–50 km/h gusts on top of it.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They will study the damage before any reopening date is set.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This is Radio BCS2050. Today a deep dive on Tourism. What does the Pacific ask back from every hotel it touches?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias reports that Hotel San Cristóbal on Punta Lobos beach in Todos Santos has suspended operations. One building and its 12 beachfront rooms were damaged by high tides.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No one was hurt.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Correct. They will assess before any reopening. It brings back questions about building on the shoreline.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the sea ask of these buildings?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The case revives debate on beach occupation and natural shoreline dynamics.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: POSTA México adds that the National Weather Service forecasts 2–3 m surf along the Pacific coast, including Todos Santos, with gusts of 30–50 km/h.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same stretch of water.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. Small boats face risks across several ports. The notice covers Guerrero Negro to López Mateos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How do visitors read these signals?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Early this month the Navy closed several ports to small craft after cold front 4.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The swell keeps its own calendar.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Economista notes Baja Ferries carries over 200,000 passengers a year on its La Paz routes and hopes to reach 300–400,000 with a cruise-style experience.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 90% of goods reach the peninsula by sea.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It has 20–30 partnerships with hotels and agencies plus an alliance with the Chepe train.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What happens to the crossing when it becomes part of the holiday itself?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: El Financiero reports Los Cabos air connections grew 61 percent in a decade. The destination expects about 3.5 million visitors this year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when the numbers keep rising while one hotel steps back?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Fiturca says private-aviation arrivals tripled and the team wants to lengthen stays through nature, food and wellness.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The light on the water stays the same.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Luz, the numbers keep pointing to one thread.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The revenue law Gringo Gazette reported, the 9 percent drop.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yes. Own-source income falling nearly 20 percent because real estate cools.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yet the same corridor still runs the airport that sets every seasonal peak.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. The portal’s earlier Foresight editions kept returning to water and grid as the ceiling.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the thread is not the events themselves but the pipes and the power that must carry them.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The East Cape road debate shows it too. Residents want the coastal route kept, while the plan weighs an alternative further inland.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Diario Humano notes the signature drive runs this week to protect that rustic path in the 2040 plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the stalled walkability projects in Cabo San Lucas sit on the same line.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meganoticias adds that the Camina Cabo plan and downtown makeover remain paused at state level.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The La Paz street rebuild under Tribuna de México aims to revive tourism there too, with concrete laid from tomorrow.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile the Shell Nurse reefs in the bay offer another thread, a fisheries answer to warming waters.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here is the turn. The Baja 1000 brought 800 million pesos and 80 percent occupancy, yet formal jobs in the state still fell 1.1 percent year on year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the hidden design is not the festival but the capacity that must last after the trucks leave.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What happens when the next tide and the next desal plant decide together?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Did you know Los Cabos lists 22,254 hotel rooms across 188 hotels?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That is a lot of beds for one stretch of coast.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Imagine the sheets changed every morning across that many rooms, all facing the same sea.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. Each one waiting for the next guest.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: SETUE put 2025 occupancy at 70.0 percent, with an average stay of 4.7 days.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So most nights the rooms are more than two thirds full.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Asociación de Hoteles de Los Cabos reported 78 percent occupancy for the first half of November 2026.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And La Paz runs at 64 percent with far fewer rooms.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. La Paz has 148 hotels and only 3,841 rooms, average stay just 2.04 days.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The southern corridor leans on those beds, yet water still limits how many more can open.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The numbers show how tightly the southern corridor leans on those beds.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal’s Vision for tourism looks at risk first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Yes. The Los Cabos engine and coastal corridor concentrate demand on water, grid and coastal ceilings. 2025 occupancy sat at 70.0 percent in Los Cabos and 64 percent in La Paz, according to SETUE. November 2026 already shows 78 percent in Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What does the portal see as the real aspiration?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Tourism kept inside water, energy and coastal limits, without cloning the Cabos model across the state. Occupancy and spending are read as signals, not volume targets.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the levers that could shift the path?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Condition new growth on real water and power margin or on a source that does not lean on NOM-011 credit. Treat beach closures as a hard limit. Move weight toward La Paz, Loreto and the interior, each with its own role.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Tendencia 2050 describes a polycentric system.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. Los Cabos under stress, East Cape in tension with protected areas, La Paz as service and energy node, Loreto as conservation anchor, Comondú with more room, and the north still thin on data.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What conditions would keep those roles distinct?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: New projects only where margin is shown. East Cape and Loreto must respect ANP and POEL ceilings first. Comondú and the north add production without draining services or protected zones. The watchlist includes Punta Lobos and the Hotel San Cristóbal case, now under Profepa review.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. What would it take for that polycentric picture to hold?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The takeaway is simple. Tourism here must stay inside the real limits of water, energy and coast, instead of cloning the Cabos model along every road south.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos gains 60% more flights yet projects a 9% revenue drop in 2027.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mm. And after the surf hit Punta Lobos, the hotel closed while crews watch the debris so none reaches the sea.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Residents are signing to keep the East Cape road in the 2040 plan.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the long road stays what it is. Stay with us. More Radio BCS2050 after the music.
